full_judgment:
10. With regard to the eligibility of respondent Nos.10 and 11 the High court Division found that those two firms had also conducted audit of one Telecom Operator in the past 3 years and, therefore, in choosing to accept their bids BTRC willfully waived the said disqualification in clear violation of the terms of the tender notice. The High Court Division further observed that just because the petitioner firm would not be able to participate in the fresh tender because of the said disqualification clause in the tender notice, it should not be disentitled to challenge the irregularity/illegality allegedly committed by the BTRC in the tender process in question. The High Court Division commented that the terms and conditions in any fresh tender notice to be published by BTRC might or might not keep the said disqualification clause and hence the writ petitioners should not be refused audience on mere hypothesis. 

 12. The High Court Division further observed that, admittedly, the petitioner firm filed its first objection before the head of the procuring entity on 28-3-2010 but the BTRC published notification of awarding contract in favour of respondent Nos. 10 and 12 in the Daily Star on 30-3-2011 in view of Rule-37, which is a clear violation of Rule 59 (2) which provides that once an objection is filed before the procuring entity, the notification of awarding contract shall not be published until the said objection is finally disposed of. The High Court Division went on to observe that "not only the notification of awarding contract has been published pending such objection; the BTRC even executed formal agreement with respondent No. 12 on 5-4-2011 and continued such violation thereafter. Again, when an interim request/order was sent by the CPTU to the BTRC on 24-4-2011 in view of Rule 59(1), the BTRC defied the same and continued to execute another formal agreement with respondent No. 11 on 26-4-2011." It was further observed that the procuring entity has the power to continue with the publication of notice of awarding con-tract once a certificate is issued by the head of the entity with prior approval of the Secretary or Minister of the concerned Ministry to the effect that the said continuation is required in-consideration of public interest, but the circular dated 2-5-2011 issued by the Chairman of BTRC does not show any such prior approval from the concerned Minister or Secretary, who expressed contrary view in their letter dated 24- 5-2011. Taking all these matters into consideration the High Court Division came to the conclusion that the decision of the Review Panel constituted by CPTU is final and binding on all concerned parties including BTRC, which attended the hearing before the Review Panel. In this regard we are of the view that the Review Panel constituted by the CPTU is part and parcel of the public Procurement Ain, 2006 and Public Procurement Bidhimala, 2008 and the decisions of such review body cannot be ignored or avoided by BTRC. We do not find any impropriety in the assessment made and decision reached by the High Court Division in this regard.
